chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about purchasing land from a Jew and a Christian.

He said: “There is no harm in it. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conquered Khaybar and made an agreement with them that the land would remain in their hands, and they would work it and cultivate it. So there is no harm if you purchase something from it. And whichever people revive a piece of land and develop it, they have the greater right to it, and it belongs to them.”

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِهِ: more entitled to it by right
key_terms.أَحْيَوْا: revived barren land and brought it into productive use
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar, the well-known territory referenced in the Prophetic precedent

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy land from Jews or Christians in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that purchasing land from Jews and Christians is permissible. It cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله at Khaybar and establishes the legal principle that those who revive and cultivate land have the strongest right to it.
